hints.title: Perimeter Calculation Obstacle
hints.text: Traversing an island of land cells requires calculating exposed boundary edges without recounting internal shared walls. How can subtracting adjacent shared borders simplify the boundary count?

hints.title: Shared Edge Subtraction Invariant
hints.text: Each isolated land cell contributes 4 edges. Each shared border between two adjacent land cells reduces the total perimeter by 2.

hints.title: Cell Edge Scan Procedure
hints.text: Iterate through every cell (r, c). If grid[r][c] == 1, add 4 to perimeter. If row r > 0 and grid[r-1][c] == 1, subtract 2. If col c > 0 and grid[r][c-1] == 1, subtract 2. Return total perimeter.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Single scan checking only top and left neighbors in O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Complex flood fills risk re-counting edges and use extra recursion space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct neighbor inspection uses constant auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using adjacent shared wall subtraction (subtracting 2) to eliminate redundant counting.
